trends.name: Iran War Exit & Oil Volatility
trends.summary: Trump signaling willingness to end Iran conflict within 4-6 weeks without reopening Strait of Hormuz, creating uncertainty around oil prices and geopolitical risk premium. Gulf allies privately pushing for continued war; conflicting signals between US, Israel, and Iran creating volatility in energy markets and Asian currency weakness.

trends.name: China Manufacturing Recovery Accelerates
trends.summary: China's Manufacturing PMI surged to 50.4 (vs 50.1 est, 49.0 prev), Non-Manufacturing PMI at 50.1, Composite at 50.5—signaling strongest factory growth in a year. Positive data counters recession fears but may pressure USD and benefit commodity-linked assets; implications for global supply chains and EM currencies.

trends.name: Semiconductor Sector Underperformance
trends.summary: Software outperforming semiconductors by >500bps (5%) today—a rare event signaling rotation away from chip stocks. Micron sank 10% post-earnings; reflects AI power demand concerns and broader semiconductor weakness amid recession fears and supply chain anxieties.

trends.name: Global Recession Risk & Market Drawdown
trends.summary: SPY down 7.1% YTD; Wall Street's 2026 'banner year' thesis collapsing as investors brace for global recession. Asian currencies weakening on oil fears; US equities faring worse than past geopolitical shocks with room to fall further. Bonds providing modest alpha as flight-to-safety continues.

trends.name: India Data Center & PE Investment Surge
trends.summary: Indian telecom giant Airtel raising $1B for data centers from Carlyle and major PE firms, signaling strong investor appetite for India's digital infrastructure. Reflects mega-trend in AI infrastructure buildout, emerging market tech growth, and PE capital rotation into essential services.

trends.name: Shipping & Logistics Disruption
trends.summary: Iran War impacting global shipping carriers; Strait of Hormuz closure risk forcing alternative routing and cost inflation. JetBlue raising checked bag fees as fuel costs surge; Sysco's $29B cash-and-carry buyout reflects consolidation amid logistics pressure.

trends.name: Gold Surge & Commodity Supply Chain
trends.summary: Barrick Mining positioned as structural opportunity; three niche commodity prices surging, revealing China's grip on critical supply chains. Geopolitical risk and recession hedging driving precious metals demand; managed money initially drove gold sell-off in January but momentum rebuilding.

trends.name: Japan Economic Weakness
trends.summary: Japan retail sales collapsed M/M -2.0% (vs -0.9% est) and Y/Y -0.2% (vs 0.8% est), signaling consumer weakness in major economy. Adds to global recession narrative and suggests weakness spreading beyond geopolitical hotspots to developed markets.

trends.name: Energy Sector Volatility & South Korea Relief
trends.summary: South Korea proposing $17B+ additional budget to ease energy costs amid Iran war uncertainty. Oil market whipsaw on conflicting Trump signals creating tradeable volatility; energy stocks sensitive to both geopolitical risk and duration expectations.

trends.name: Sector Rotation & Valuation Reset
trends.summary: Multiple stocks experiencing 'valuation resets' post-selloff: State Street undervalued opportunity, Willdan margin strength, Janus International more attractive cheaper, Fox Factory turnaround. Investors hunting for quality compounders at depressed prices; defensive positioning evident (bonds outperforming).

trends.name: AI & Software Investment Opportunities
trends.summary: Tempus AI attractive entry point; Private Equity ETF BUYO addresses AI software disruption risk vs illiquid alts; China's AI race entering new phase. Software outperformance today signals capital rotating to AI-pure plays as hardware faces headwinds.

trends.name: US Tax & Consumer Spending Headwinds
trends.summary: Retirement saver protection rule dead for second time, creating planning uncertainty. Tax refund delays hitting restaurant and retail spending; NY Governor facing $17B+ tax increase pressure from 30 organizations. Consumer spending weakness and policy uncertainty weighing on discretionary sectors.
